chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abu al-Maghra', from Zayd al-Shahham, from Amr ibn Sa'id ibn Hilal, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I do not meet you except in [long] years, so advise me with something so that I may adopt it.'
He said, 'I advise you to be mindful of Allah, to practice piety, and to strive [in worship]. And beware of aspiring to the position of one who is above you.'
And sufficient is what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, told His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family): 'Do not impress you their wealth and their children.'
And He said: 'And do not extend your gaze [yearningly] at what We have provided their groups of the embellishment of the life of this world.'

If you fear any of this [happening to you], then recall the life of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for his sustenance was from barley, his sweetness from dates, and his fuel was palm fronds if he found them.

And if a calamity befalls you in your self, or your wealth, or your child, then recall your calamity with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for the creatures have never been afflicted with anything like it.

key_terms.عِيشَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The life/sustenance of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What advice did Imam al-Sadiq give for maintaining spiritual balance and contentment?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises the narrator to cultivate *war'* (piety) and *ijtihad* (striving) while avoiding *tamuhh* (excessive aspiration for worldly status), grounding this advice in Quranic verses about not being dazzled by wealth and progeny. He further encourages contentment by recalling the Prophet’s simple sustenance of barley and dates, linking material simplicity to spiritual elevation. Finally, he instructs the believer to use the Prophet’s sufferings as a source of consolation during personal trials, emphasizing the unique magnitude of his sacrifices.
